records.:topic/title: Calculating the Inverse of a 3x3 Matrix Using the Cofactor Method
The Determinant of an NxN Matrix

records.:question/worked-solution:
Given a $2\times 2$ matrix

$$
C=\begin{bmatrix}a & b \\ c & d\end{bmatrix},
$$

the inverse of $C$ can be found using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{det(C)}\begin{bmatrix}d & -b \\ -c & a\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we compute the determinant:

$$
det(C)=(-5)\cdot 5-(-2)\cdot 10=-5
$$

Using the formula, then, the inverse is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{det(C)}\begin{bmatrix}d & -b \\ -c & a\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-5)}\begin{bmatrix}5 & -10 \\ 2 & -5\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 2 \\ -2/5 & 1\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can verify the result as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}C{C}^{-1} & =\begin{bmatrix}-5 & 10 \\ -2 & 5\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 2 \\ -2/5 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & ={I}_{2}\,✓ \\ {C}^{-1}C & =\begin{bmatrix}-1 & 2 \\ -2/5 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}-5 & 10 \\ -2 & 5\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & ={I}_{2}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
